problem: Existing continual category discovery methods assume stationary data distributions, failing in realistic open-world scenarios where data comes from shifting domains.
approach: PRISM uses high-frequency spectral components to distinguish known from unknown categories, sparse assignment matching for reliable clustering, and domain-invariant knowledge transfer to handle distribution shifts.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on SSB-C and DomainNet benchmarks by addressing non-stationary open-world continual discovery.

problem: Understanding the geometric structure of how LLMs encode conceptual knowledge and logical operations in embedding space remains unclear.
approach: Unifies the Linear Representation Hypothesis with Formal Concept Analysis to show that LLM embeddings induce concept lattices via half-space intersections, enabling symbolic reasoning through geometric meet and join operations.
contribution: Empirically demonstrates that LLM embeddings encode concept lattices, bridging continuous geometry and symbolic abstraction through lattice geometry.

problem: Multi-agent systems struggle to optimize interactions and collaboration among agents for complex reasoning tasks.
approach: AgentPO employs reinforcement learning to train a specialized Collaborator agent that refines its interaction policy to enhance overall system performance within a fixed multi-agent topology.
contribution: Achieves accuracy improvements of +1.8% to +7.2% on mathematical reasoning with only 500 training samples while operating at 7.8% of baseline inference cost.

problem: Difficult examples near decision boundaries, crucial in supervised learning, are assumed to be essential for contrastive learning but their actual role is poorly understood.
approach: Develops a theoretical framework modeling sample similarity to show difficult examples negatively affect contrastive learning generalization; proposes efficient mechanisms for removing these examples and tuning margins/temperature.
contribution: Shows removing difficult examples can boost downstream classification performance despite reducing sample size, with theory and empirical validation.

problem: Learning from multi-variate time-series with heterogeneous channel configurations is challenging, especially in clinical domains like intracranial EEG where setups vary widely across subjects.
approach: Introduces multi-variate parallel attention (MVPA), a self-attention mechanism that disentangles content, temporal, and spatial attention, enabling flexible modeling of variable channel counts and configurations.
contribution: MVPFormer foundation model surpasses state-of-the-art on seizure detection and achieves expert-level performance on four Brain TreeBank iEEG decoding tasks (volume, pitch, onset, speech).

problem: Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons assume linear current summation but biological neurons integrate inputs nonlinearly, limiting the computational expressivity of spiking neural networks.
approach: Proposes Dendritic LIF (DLIF) model incorporating bilinear dendritic integration derived from neurophysiology, enabling nonlinear computation and preserving correlation structures across layers.
contribution: DLIF achieves state-of-the-art performance on static (CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet) and neuromorphic (DVS-Gesture, DVS-CIFAR10) benchmarks while maintaining comparable computational cost.

problem: Creating high-quality scientific illustrations is a well-recognized bottleneck in both academia and industry, yet automated approaches are lacking.
approach: AutoFigure is an agentic framework that generates scientific illustrations from long-form text through extensive thinking, recombination, and validation stages to produce structurally sound and aesthetically refined layouts.
contribution: Surpasses all baseline methods on FigureBench (3,300 text-figure pairs) to produce publication-ready scientific illustrations.

problem: Traditional multimodal learning relies heavily on large paired datasets, but vast unpaired multimodal data remains unexploited for enhancing target unimodal representations.
approach: UML is a modality-agnostic paradigm where a single model alternately processes inputs from different modalities while sharing parameters, exploiting the assumption that modalities are projections of shared underlying reality.
contribution: Theoretically shows unpaired auxiliary data yields representations strictly more informative than unimodal training; empirically improves downstream performance across diverse unimodal targets.

problem: Understanding how momentum and adaptive step-sizes affect the convergence and generalization of stochastic gradient descent in high-dimensional settings is poorly understood.
approach: Develops high-dimensional scaling limits for SGD with Polyak Momentum and adaptive step-sizes, enabling rigorous comparison with vanilla SGD through time rescaling and step-size analysis.
contribution: Demonstrates that SGD-M with adaptive step-sizes achieves fixed points closer to population minimum and widens admissible step-size ranges, providing rigorous account of high-dimensional effects.

problem: Evaluating motion correction methods in MRI is fundamentally difficult due to lack of accessible ground-truth target data.
approach: Studies three evaluation approaches (real-world with reference scans, simulated motion, reference-free) and releases PMoC3D dataset; introduces MoMRISim, a feature-space metric trained for evaluating motion reconstructions.
contribution: Demonstrates real-world evaluation with MoMRISim is most reliable, showing simulated motion overestimates performance and reference-free evaluation overrates smoothed deep learning outputs.

problem: Open-source models struggle with large-scale, diverse-format data files and long-horizon multi-step reasoning required for real-world data analytics.
approach: DataMind applies fine-grained task taxonomy, recursive task composition, knowledge-augmented sampling, and dynamically adjustable SFT+RL training on DataMind-12K, a high-quality trajectory dataset.
contribution: DataMind-14B achieves 71.16% on multiple data analysis benchmarks, outperforming proprietary baselines DeepSeek-V3.1 and GPT-5; DataMind-7B best among open-source at 68.10%.

problem: Learning game mechanics (modular rules governing gameplay) from video rather than mere visual reproduction remains unexplored.
approach: Formalizes mechanic-learning as a causal counterfactual inference task grounded in causal consistency principle; introduces Multiverse Mechanica testbed that emits training data paired with causal DAGs.
contribution: Provides reproducible, low-cost testbed for studying and comparing methods to learn game mechanics beyond pixel reproduction.

problem: Positive-unlabeled learning evaluation is highly inconsistent across studies, making it difficult to identify which algorithm performs better and fairly compare different problem settings.
approach: Proposes first PU learning benchmark with systematic evaluation; investigates model selection without negative data; identifies internal label shift in one-sample setting and proposes calibration approach.
contribution: Provides accessible, realistic, and fair framework for evaluating PU learning algorithms within and across different problem families.

problem: Reinforcement learning for LLMs remains extremely costly due to expensive rollout stages, and allowing actor-policy distribution mismatch could improve scalability but creates stability-performance trade-offs.
approach: Jackpot leverages Optimal Budget Rejection Sampling to reduce actor-policy distribution gaps, with efficient probability estimation via Top-K logits and stabilized PPO loss accounting for both importance sampling and trust regions.
contribution: Achieves 20% improvement on AMC and ~8% on AIME benchmarks under extreme off-policy training (128× ratio for Qwen3-4B) with improved stability over baselines.

problem: Evaluation practices for LLMs in single-cell biology are inadequate with fragmented, format-mismatched benchmarks and metrics lacking biological grounding.
approach: SC-Arena introduces a virtual cell abstraction unifying evaluation targets; defines five natural language tasks (annotation, captioning, generation, perturbation prediction, QA); proposes knowledge-augmented evaluation using ontologies and literature.
contribution: Demonstrates current models achieve uneven performance on biologically complex tasks requiring mechanistic or causal understanding.

problem: Multi-modal reasoning models can infer precise geographic locations from personal images through hierarchical reasoning, posing significant privacy risks not addressed by perception-only protection methods.
approach: ReasonBreak uses concept-aware adversarial perturbations targeting critical conceptual dependencies within reasoning chains to disrupt geographic inference while maintaining interpretability.
contribution: Achieves 14.4% improvement in tract-level protection (33.8% vs 19.4%) and nearly doubles block-level protection (33.5% vs 16.8%) across seven state-of-the-art MLRMs.

problem: Designing efficient and numerically stable metrics for Symmetric Positive Definite matrix learning in Riemannian neural networks is challenging.
approach: Exploits Cholesky decomposition to uncover product structure, proposing Power-Cholesky Metric (PCM) and Bures-Wasserstein-Cholesky Metric (BWCM) with closed-form operators and improved stability.
contribution: Provides computationally efficient, numerically stable metrics with applications to Riemannian MLR classifiers and residual blocks for SPD neural networks.

problem: LLMs can produce seemingly correct legal judgments while relying on incorrect inference patterns, but methods to audit detailed inference correctness are lacking.
approach: Quantifies interactions between input phrases used by LLMs as primitive inference patterns and evaluates them using interaction-based explanation metrics grounded in theoretical guarantees.
contribution: Shows significant portions of LLM inference patterns for legal judgment may represent misleading or irrelevant logic despite correct outputs.

problem: Camera-centric understanding and generation are studied separately, and existing methods lack effective paradigms to align camera parameters with visual reasoning.
approach: Puffin treats camera as language, enabling spatial reasoning through camera terminology while interpreting and generating scenes from arbitrary viewpoints using language regression and diffusion.
contribution: Trained on Puffin-4M (4 million vision-language-camera triplets), outperforms specialized models on camera-centric tasks and generalizes to diverse cross-view tasks.

problem: Ultrasound images have unique texture and structural attributes with scarce large-scale datasets, hindering effective application of conventional machine learning methods.
approach: ARL proposes anatomy-adaptive Vision Transformer (A-ViT) self-supervised learning framework parameterized with large-scale medical ultrasound dataset to provide anatomy-aware feature representations.
contribution: Significantly outperforms self-supervised baselines across ultrasound diagnostic tasks including breast/thyroid cancer, cardiac view classification, and COVID-19 identification.

problem: 3D Large Language Models typically lack explicit reasoning processes in training data, limiting complex spatial reasoning and task planning capabilities.
approach: SCoT annotates a million-scale Chain-of-Thought dataset across three levels: spatial perception, analysis, and planning, with intermediate reasoning grounded in scene cues.
contribution: Shows CoT supervision greatly benefits complex analysis and planning but can induce hallucinations in simple perception tasks, highlighting nuanced challenges of scene-grounded reasoning.

problem: Existing Dynamic Text-Attributed Graph datasets suffer from poor textual quality and lack standardized task formulations for generative DyTAG tasks.
approach: GDGB provides eight curated DyTAG datasets with high-quality textual features and defines two novel tasks: Transductive (TDGG) and Inductive (IDGG) Dynamic Graph Generation, with multifaceted evaluation metrics.
contribution: Enables rigorous evaluation of DyTAG generation through standardized benchmarks and an LLM-based multi-agent framework for reproducible benchmarking.

problem: Current visual table understanding benchmarks rely on synthetic renderings lacking complexity of real-world tables and offer no access to underlying serialized data for reformulation.
approach: TABLET provides 4 million examples across 21 tasks grounded in 2 million unique tables with 88% original visualizations; introduces VisualTableQA requiring joint visual and tabular reasoning.
contribution: Fine-tuning vision-language models on TABLET improves performance on seen/unseen VTU tasks while increasing robustness on real-world table visualizations.

problem: Semi-supervised federated learning assumes labeled and unlabeled data share the same label space, but realistic scenarios contain outliers from absent categories.
approach: FedOpenMatch addresses open-set semi-supervised federated learning (OSSFL) using one-vs-all classifier as outlier detector with logit adjustment and gradient stop, plus logit consistency regularization.
contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on standard benchmarks across diverse data settings for open-set semi-supervised federated learning.

problem: Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation on Markov Random Fields with locally sparse connections is computationally challenging due to cycles in the graph structure.
approach: Samples uniform random spanning trees from MRF graphs to break cycles and decompose MAP inference into overlapping tree sub-problems that can be solved exactly and efficiently.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on synthetic, UAI inference competition, and real-world PCI problems, especially for locally sparse connected graphs.

problem: Deepfake detection benchmarks suffer from severe discrepancies with industrial practice, featuring homogeneous sources and low-quality testing images, limiting real-world applicability.
approach: Veritas is an MLLM-based detector using pattern-aware reasoning (planning and self-reflection) instead of vanilla chain-of-thought, trained via two-stage pipeline to internalize deepfake reasoning.
contribution: Achieves significant gains across out-of-domain scenarios (unseen forgeries, data domains, model architectures) with transparent, faithful detection outputs.

problem: Goal-conditioned reinforcement learning requires careful reward design, and existing methods struggle with complex dynamics and long-horizon planning.
approach: Eik-HiQRL reformulates Quasimetric RL via Eikonal PDEs for trajectory-free learning, then integrates it into a hierarchical decomposition to handle complex dynamics limitations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on offline goal-conditioned navigation and consistent gains over QRL in manipulation, matching temporal-difference methods.

problem: Locating relevant theorems and learning Lean is hindered by difficulty in finding theorems and steep language learning curve, slowing formal theorem proving progress.
approach: Lean Finder uses user-centered semantic search by analyzing Lean discussions, fine-tuning embeddings on synthesized queries, and aligning with mathematician preferences via feedback signals.
contribution: Achieves over 30% relative improvement compared to previous search engines and GPT-4o; compatible with LLM-based theorem provers.

problem: Foundation models for EEG are emerging but their true advantages over traditional methods in diverse BCI tasks and data-scarce scenarios remain unclear.
approach: Comprehensive benchmark of EEG foundation models across datasets, tasks, and evaluation protocols with rigorous statistics; introduces ST-EEGFormer baseline using masked autoencoding on 8M segments.
contribution: Shows fine-tuned foundation models often fail to significantly outperform classical decoders in data-scarce settings, exposing gap between pre-training and downstream fine-tuning.

problem: Scientific time series presents unique challenges where encoding as text or images is insufficient due to long sequences and precision loss, limiting multimodal LLM capabilities.
approach: SciTS introduces a benchmark spanning 12 domains with 50k+ instances and signals from 10^0 to 10^7 in length; benchmarks 17 models and proposes TimeOmni to extend LLMs for scientific time series.
contribution: Shows general-purpose LLMs have stronger generalizability than specialized models; TimeOmni explores how to extend LLMs for scientific time series while maintaining general-purpose training.

problem: Spoken language models lack internal unspoken thinking processes, unlike humans who engage in complex mental reasoning before speaking, causing inefficient or lower-quality responses.
approach: STITCH alternates between unspoken reasoning chunks and spoken response chunks, using the time taken to play audio response chunks to generate reasoning tokens simultaneously.
contribution: Matches latency of baselines without reasoning while outperforming them by 15% on math reasoning datasets, enabling simultaneous thinking and talking.

problem: LLMs as world models suffer from hallucination and reliance on static training knowledge, leading to compounding errors in long-horizon simulations for computer-use agents.
approach: R-WoM grounds LLM simulations by retrieving factual, up-to-date knowledge from external tutorials to enhance future state prediction and reward estimation.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements of up to 25.3% (OSWorld) and 18.1% (WebArena) compared to baselines, with particular advantage in longer-horizon simulations.

problem: Graph Neural Networks struggle to balance cost-effectiveness and global receptive field when learning long-distance knowledge across graph structures.
approach: FGL reinterprets message passing as transportation over spanning trees, where a forest of trees captures complementary topological pathways with improved edge-homophily estimation.
contribution: Achieves comparable results to state-of-the-art on semi-supervised node classification while remaining efficient with linear-time tree aggregation.

problem: Diffusion Transformers for video generation suffer from inherent sequential denoising causing inevitable latency, limiting real-world applicability.
approach: BWCache dynamically caches and reuses DiT block features across diffusion timesteps when feature variations fall below similarity threshold, using U-shaped pattern to identify redundancy.
contribution: Achieves up to 2.24× speedup with comparable visual quality on several video diffusion models through training-free acceleration.

problem: Transformer probabilistic models excel at single-pass marginal prediction but generating coherent joint distributions requires expensive re-encoding at each autoregressive step.
approach: Introduces a causal autoregressive buffer that processes context once and caches it, while a dynamic buffer captures target dependencies enabling efficient batched generation.
contribution: Matches predictive accuracy of strong baselines while delivering up to 20× faster joint sampling across synthetic functions, signals, and tabular data.

problem: Theoretical understanding of the expressive power of diagonal State-Space Models on sequential state-tracking tasks remains limited.
approach: Studies input-dependent complex-valued diagonal SSMs, proving single-layer can track any Abelian group but not non-Abelian groups, and k-layer models track groups with subnormal series of length k.
contribution: Establishes tight expressivity bounds for DCD SSMs; empirically reveals gap between theoretical expressivity and practical learnability for non-Abelian groups.

problem: Diffusion language models promise faster parallel inference but their theoretical foundations and optimality properties remain unestablished.
approach: Formalizes a model of parallel sampling and proves DLMs with polynomial-length chain-of-thought can simulate any parallel algorithm optimally, with revision enabling optimal space complexity.
contribution: Provides theoretical justification for DLMs as efficient samplers and establishes strict expressivity gap showing revision is necessary for optimal performance.

problem: Intermediate fusion multimodal learning lacks sufficient theoretical analysis comparing its generalization to late fusion approaches.
approach: Revisits IF and LF from fine-grained perspective, derives generalization error upper bounds showing IF superiority under specific constraints, and proposes IF-based method with informatic constraints.
contribution: Establishes theoretical evidence for IF superiority; demonstrates eliminating distribution incoherence improves IF-based MML generalizability.

problem: Out-of-distribution robustness in causal representation learning from interventional image pairs needs better approaches focusing on intervention representation.
approach: Proposes Causal Delta Embeddings that represent interventions invariantly to visual scene and sparsely in terms of affected causal variables, enabling learning from image pairs without supervision.
contribution: Significantly exceeds baseline performance in OOD settings on Causal Triplet challenge for both synthetic and real-world benchmarks.

problem: Audio generation methods face trade-offs: GANs suffer from slow convergence and mode collapse, while diffusion methods require costly multi-step inference.
approach: Flow2GAN combines Flow Matching training with GAN fine-tuning for few-step inference, using endpoint estimation and spectral energy-based loss for audio, plus multi-resolution network architecture.
contribution: Delivers high-fidelity audio generation with better quality-efficiency trade-offs than existing GAN-based and Flow Matching methods, enabling one-step generation.
